submitted.rationale: Index 13 (Bi0.75Sb0.25, the Bi3SbO7 stoichiometry) gave the highest measured EQE, 0.0052%. Bi3SbO7 is on the MACE hull, and its MEGNet HSE gap of 2.27 eV absorbs 3.2 eV light. The Bi-rich end (index 1) and the BiSbO4 point (index 21) both measured lower, so EQE peaks somewhere in between.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.0014%: the Bi2O3-rich end performs worse.
Measured EQE 0.0030%: BiSbO4's gap (~2.9-3.1 eV) sits near the 3.2 eV photon energy, so it absorbs weakly.
Not measured because the budget ran out. It lies between two measured points that both fell short of index 13.

consultations.verdict: Support: Bi3SbO7 (Sb 0.25) is on the MACE hull and MEGNet HSE gap 2.27 eV < 3.2 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; index 13 (Sb 0.249) sits at this stoichiometry.

Support: alpha-Bi2O3 is on the hull with an HSE gap of 2.34 eV, so it absorbs 3.2 eV light. The Bi-rich end (lightly Sb-doped Bi2O3 or sillenite) is the untested alternative after the low EQE at Bi3SbO7.

Support: BiSbO4 is stable (on hull earlier) with a gap of ~2.9–3.06 eV, just under 3.2 eV, and it is a known photocatalyst. EQE went up from Bi-rich (0.0014) to Sb 0.25 (0.0052), so the Sb-richer BiSbO4 composition is the best remaining bet.
